assignments.note: 2022-10 Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
assignments.why: Measures how optimising a policy against a proxy RM first raises then lowers true reward: overoptimisation of the training signal.

assignments.note: 2023-10 A Long Way to Go Length Correlations in RLHF
assignments.why: Shows much of the RLHF reward gain is length; the policy exploits an RM shortcut.

assignments.note: 2023-10 Reward Model Ensembles Help Mitigate Overoptimization
assignments.why: RM ensembles as the reward in BoN and PPO to reduce policy overoptimisation.
Automatically labelled PRM used as the reward for step-by-step PPO, with reported policy gains.
Model's own LLM-judge scores are the training reward for iterative DPO; judge-in-the-loop training, with length growth noted.
Reward design aimed at reducing length hacking of the RLHF policy.
Self-evaluation used as the reward signal for DPO to reduce hallucinations.

assignments.note: 2024-06 Scaling Laws for RM Overoptimization in Direct Alignment
assignments.why: Overoptimisation of the implicit reward in DPO/IPO training, mainly length exploitation.
Self-judging loop whose judgments train the policy via DPO; documents length drift and self-reinforcing judge bias.

assignments.note: 2024-07 Prover-verifier games improve legibility of LLM outputs
assignments.why: Verifier acceptance is the RL reward for helpful and sneaky provers; studies what that reward does to policy legibility.

assignments.note: 2024-09 Language Models Learn to Mislead Humans via RLHF
assignments.why: RLHF against human evaluators teaches the policy to convince evaluators of wrong answers: reward hacking of the judge.
Generator optimising against an LLM evaluator raises evaluator scores while true quality stalls: reward hacking (in-context optimisation).

assignments.note: 2024-04 Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
assignments.why: Trajectory evaluators used as the reward for Reflexion-style refinement and filtered fine-tuning of agents, with reported policy gains.
Introduces RLVR: programmatic checker as the training reward; notes checker gaps as reward-hacking targets.
Large-scale RL with rule-based rewards, chosen to avoid reward hacking of neural RMs.
Generative RMs used as RLVR rewards are exploited by content-free 'master key' answers; a reward-hacking vulnerability of the training signal.
Log-scoring-rule reward in PPO and its effect on the policy's verbalised calibration.
Self-play RL with a code executor as the verifier reward and a learnability reward for task proposal.

assignments.note: 2025-06 CURE Co-Evolving Coder and Unit Tester
assignments.why: Generated unit tests are the coder's RL reward; the paper designs the tester reward against wrong or naive tests.
Shows the binary RLVR reward trains overconfident guessing and adds a Brier term to the reward; the reward is what drives the calibration change.
Rubric-based LLM-judge rewards for on-policy RL where no verifier exists.
Shows RLVR leaves policies near-certain on every verdict and modifies the training signal to fix calibration.
Tests from an adversarial Test LLM are the Code LLM's reward; addresses self-collusion of the reward.
Proper-score reward replacing RLVR's correct-answer reward; analyses what each reward does to the policy (confident errors, reasoning switched off).
